title: Import changed task-sync files with constant Git starts
outcome: Apply only changed task-sync planning from the recorded committed basis, with a constant Git process count independent of total and changed tasks
acceptance: An ordinary import starts from the recorded last-applied commit or the confirmed own export commit for this project and profile. One raw Git diff to the incoming tip selects changed paths, modes and new object IDs. Read only required changed A/M JSON and graph support from the clean worktree or one shared streaming Git reader with no chunks. If the import needs Git bodies for selected memory or evidence inputs, it uses the same stream. Apply task removals from the diff.

Use the keyed SQLite comparison baseline and indexed feed cut to admit changed planning and report conflicts. Check exact Git paths, ordinary file modes, new values and the selected tip before applying. Preserve held-task admission, local changes owed to the next export, and complete-publication subtree identity through the export owner's recorded basis contract.

An ordinary import performs no per-file publication history search or speculative adoption. An unconfirmed, discarded or altered own export, or a missing, stale, gapped or inconsistent basis, gives a typed refusal with the explicit recovery. A complete read is limited to empty bootstrap or a named rebuild with its own saved basis.

Deterministic Git-start hook tests assert identical ordinary-import process counts on the same route for K=1, 100 and 2,000 changed tasks at N=2,000, and for the same change set at N=200 and N=2,000. Include zero-blob and positive selected-blob controls, assert that unrelated task documents stay unopened, and record the counts on the parent item.
